newsitem.title: USA: Senate Leader Lott hopeful of budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Senate Leader Lott hopeful of budget pact.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he had spoken to budget negotiators Monday and was "hopeful" that an agreement could be reached with the White House this week.

He said that Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, and House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican, were both "pretty upbeat" about the status of budget talks. "They still feel like they might get something done here in the next couple of days and so ... I'm hopeful," the Mississippi Republican told reporters.
Budget talks were expected to go on Monday night and Tuesday morning, Lott said, "we hope to get an agreement on a budget."

On fast-track trade negotiation authority, Lott said he has made clear to the Clinton administration "we are not going to have an agreement that mandates certain labour or environmental concerns." If the administration acknowledges that, "we can get this agreement worked out I think early in the summer," he said.

Fast-track legislation would allow U.S. trade officials to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile and other market-opening trade accords without fear the pacts will be revised by Congress.

However, if putting together a budget is delayed, that could also delay consideration of fast-track authority, Lott said. "Everything is going to be affected this year by what we do or don't do in the budget area," he added.
